judgments.reasoning_cat1: An acknowledgment clause; 'solely to ensure the quality' is a characterisation rather than an operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It echoes §13's identical explanation of Licensor's supervisory powers and constrains the reach of 4(b)-(c) and 5(a), but I found no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitrable class — disputes 'regarding the failure of Licensee to conform to any provision of quality control' — has genuinely contestable edges, 'substantial failure' is vague, and 'proscribed' for 'prescribed' is a mechanical error; the alternating California/New York forum is also indeterminate as to who elects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its mandatory arbitration must be reconciled with 5(d)'s exclusion of everything 'not specifically identified hereinabove,' §14's requirement that claims be prosecuted in New York courts, and 11(a)'s grant of court injunctive relief for 'any breach,' which includes quality breaches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but plainly drafted remedial powers; 'deemed appropriate under the circumstances' is discretionary rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The arbitrator's injunctive power overlaps with 11(a)'s court-ordered injunctions and with §14's forum clause, an allocation the contract never resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite timing and finality provision; nothing to construe beyond the directory nature of the thirty-day deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with §14's New York law choice and 5(a)-(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is a pure general-versus-specific construct: everything 'not specifically identified hereinabove, including but not limited to' validity claims is excluded from arbitration, so the reach of the exclusion depends entirely on how narrowly 5(a)'s quality-control category is read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read together with 5(a), 11(a) and §14 it produces a bifurcated dispute regime whose line — quality disputes to arbitration, all else to New York courts — is exactly the kind of allocation parties fight over, and 3(b)'s no-challenge covenant sits oddly beside its express contemplation of validity litigation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best efforts to protect' the marks is a one-line, wholly indeterminate standard with no metric, no cost cap and no procedure attached.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the detailed and differently-calibrated enforcement machinery in 6(d) (each party may sue at its own cost) and the separate best-efforts registration duty in 2(b)(iii), so its independent content is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but internally consistent prohibition; 'affect the ownership of' is broad yet workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2(b)(iii) expressly permits Licensee to prepare and file documentation as Licensor's agent if Licensor defaults, which is a carve-out this absolute prohibition does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso 'only as expressly provided herein in clause 2(b)' followed by a blanket bar on merchandise 'bearing such designations' is awkward and its antecedent ('such designations') is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The merchandise ban collides with 2(b)(vii)-(viii), which expressly permit sales of merchandise bearing the Exhibit D/E designations for eighteen months, and with 2(b)(iv)'s regime for Licensed Products.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says each party may sue 'at its own cost and expense and any monies recovered will be for the account of such party,' then that in 'joint proceedings' Licensor has full control and recoveries are 'divided equally,' without defining what makes a proceeding joint.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The equal-division rule for territory infringements is hard to square with 9(b)'s promise that Licensee is 'solely entitled to all economic benefits' of the licensed rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity runs to 'any suits, loss and damage arising out of any service or act ... in connection with this Agreement, or in relation to the Hard Rock Hotel Marks,' a catch-all so broad and one-sided that its reach (including Licensor's own conduct) is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is unilateral while 6(d) contemplates each party bearing its own enforcement costs and 11(a) gives Licensee its own remedies, but no clause squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When practical and appropriate' is an unmeasurable trigger, and the display must be 'reasonably acceptable to Licensor' although it is Licensor that must display material promoting Licensee's facilities — an apparent mechanical error for 'Licensee' that changes who controls the content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges Licensor to promote Licensee's facilities in the Morton Territories, which must be read with 8(a)(3), 8(b) and the 2(a) territorial limits; the mismatch of 'Hard Rock Facilities' (a defined term covering both parties' properties) adds strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific, concrete attribution obligation triggered by 'any book written or sponsored by Licensor or its affiliates'; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument addresses attribution or publications; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Same size and style' is a concrete, testable requirement; the qualifier 'which identifies all locations' is a slight limitation but clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits alongside 8(a)(1) and 8(b) without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Agree to discuss the possibility' is an agreement to agree with no ascertainable obligation, which is a real vagueness point though an unlikely one to be litigated alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes nothing that could conflict with any other clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'Licensor may ... except that Licensee may' structure leaves the exclusivity of each party's web rights uncertain, and 'other Hard Rock Facilities as they may develop' is loose given that the defined term already includes Licensee's properties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Licensee's web page is confined to the Morton Territories although 2(a) permits worldwide promotion and 2(b)(v) permits Internet sales bearing 'the Internet address as the Licensed Products' location'; the internet is not territorial, so the three provisions do not sit comfortably together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A license granted in perpetuity' is short and emphatic; the heading 'Term and Options' promises options that the text never provides.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Perpetuity with no termination machinery is hard to reconcile with §16 (survival of provisions after 'the termination of this Agreement') and 3(b)'s reference to 'the Term of this Agreement or thereafter'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Royalty free and fully paid' is definite; 'solely entitled to all economic benefits' is a sweeping phrase whose scope is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That sweeping entitlement is contradicted in part by 6(d) (recoveries divided equally in the Territories) and 3(c) (goodwill inures solely to Licensor).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are murky: 'all or substantially all of his assets and/or rights,' 'initiate negotiations' as the clock-starter, and a six-month re-offer trigger keyed to whether Licensee 'has not agreed to consummate a Transaction'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts transfers while §10 lets Licensee sublicense or franchise 'any or all' rights and §18 binds 'transferees and assigns,' so a near-total sublicense could bypass the first-offer right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unrestricted right to sublicense or franchise 'any or all of the rights,' with no consent requirement, coupled with a flow-down obligation whose adequacy ('assume, observe and perform all of the obligations') is broadly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unfettered sublicensing right can hollow out 9(c)'s first-offer right and sits against Licensor's quality-control and inspection rights in 4(b)-(c), which reach only 'Licensee'; §7's indemnity does contemplate sublicensees, so the fit is partial.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Careful and detailed; the acknowledgments are stipulations rather than ambiguous terms, though 'as applicable and appropriate' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Court injunctions for 'any breach of this Agreement' overlap the mandatory arbitration of quality disputes in 5(a) and the arbitrator's injunctive power in 5(b), an allocation the contract does not expressly resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard non-waiver language, mutual and clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §22 requires waivers to be in a signed writing, which reinforces rather than contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deemed-receipt rules are clear, though telecopy notice 'when receipt acknowledged' leaves delivery in the recipient's hands.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The address block names 'Hard Rock Cafe International (DEL), Inc.' as Licensor while the parties clause and 1(n) identify Rank Licensing, Inc., an inconsistency the successors language only partly cures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says 'under no circumstances shall any power be granted' to Licensee immediately after excepting Section 2(b)(iii), an internal contradiction within the clause itself, and 'use the name or credit of Licensor in any manner whatsoever' is impossibly broad in a trademark licence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The flat bar on using Licensor's name cannot be squared with the whole point of the grant in 2(a) and the marking duties in 4(e), and the agency carve-out points back to 2(b)(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear choice of New York substantive law with a forum clause; the only softness is whether 'shall be prosecuted in' is exclusive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'except as provided in Section 5' carve-out largely harmonises it with arbitration, but 5(a)'s alternating California/New York arbitral seat and 5(d)'s residual court clause still require reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate severability, clearly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision qualifies it; nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Which, in order to be effective, or by its nature, must survive' identifies no provisions and leaves the surviving set entirely to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a termination that 9(a)'s perpetual licence never provides for, and the contract contains no termination clause at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It integrates 'this Agreement together with the Purchase and Sale Agreement' without defining or dating that document, and 'with respect to the subject matter hereof' is narrower than the extinguishment sentence that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause extinguishes rights under the 1985 and 1995 settlement agreements while 2(a) warrants title 'subject only to whatever actions or inactions may have been taken ... by Morton ... prior to the date of this Agreement,' a residue the integration clause does not address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary binding-effect language; 'as the case may be' is filler rather than ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It benefits 'transferees and assigns' without carving out the transfer restraints implied by 9(c)'s first-offer right, a mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard authority representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the title warranty in 2(a) and §20; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate enforceability with a conventional bankruptcy/equity qualifier; 'its respective terms' is a stray plural but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with §§15, 19 and the rest of the boilerplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to 'the Morton Parties' and 'the Rank Parties,' terms nowhere defined in this Agreement, which is a drafting error imported from another document and leaves the representation's subjects uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parties here are defined as Licensor and Licensee in the preamble and 1(n), and the list of definitions contains no such terms, so the clause does not fit the instrument it sits in.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear formality requirement; 'entitled to the benefit thereof' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 11(b)'s non-waiver clause and §23's writing requirement rather than conflicting with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Including 'interpreted' among the things that may be done 'only by written instrument duly executed by each of the parties' is an odd and arguably self-defeating word in an amendment clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §17 already contains a no-oral-modification rule and §22 governs waivers, so the three overlap without contradicting each other.
